clue.text: Bound to have confidence in pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is taken as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to have confidence in someone is to trust them

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to have faith in an official statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but 'Bound' is the definition: tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trussed is tied up tightly, so bound is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Article about that is very appropriate

indicators.note: about means going around, so the article encloses the other letters

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A determiner, that is, being highly suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it without permission, which is to steal.

clue.text: Subjected to work experience

parts.note: under means subject to, as under orders
to go is to work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Made to do a placement as a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work experience' reads as a placement; split it so 'work' gives GO and 'experience' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or endure it.

clue.text: Don't give up, as veteran runs into youngster

indicators.note: into means the old-timer and runs go inside the young person

parts.note: a son is a youngster
an oldie is an old person or veteran
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An old soldier rushes into a boy, telling him to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to persevere in spite of difficulty, the opposite of giving up.

clue.text: Arrange band for section of theatre

parts.note: to dress is to arrange, as in dressing a window display
a band or ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Set up a group to play for part of a play's run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but means a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress circle is the first gallery of seats above the stalls in a theatre.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement excels with pressure on king

parts.note: to excel is to top, so excels gives tops
in chess a pin is pressure that holds a piece in line with the king

explanation.surface: An uprising does well once the monarch is squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary movement' suggests politics; it is the spin on a ball that makes it rotate forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward rotation given to a ball, literally a revolving motion.

clue.text: Find sum, a little one

definitions.meaning: to add up a column of figures
a young child or small measure

explanation.surface: A child counting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add figures together, and a tot is a small child or small drink.

clue.text: Food in Dad's Army?

parts.note: Pa is father, so Dad's gives Pa's
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Rations eaten by the Home Guard in a classic sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard; the question mark warns that the title is being split rather than read whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta, such as spaghetti or penne, is a staple food.

clue.text: In disorder, riot cop covered entrance

indicators.note: in disorder means jumbled up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: During a disturbance, a police officer guarded the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In disorder' rearranges RIOT COP.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with a roof supported by columns at a building's entrance.

clue.text: Pound included in coinage for western region

indicators.note: included in means the pound goes inside the coinage

parts.note: a coinage is a new word invented
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: Sterling became part of a currency for the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coinage' suggests money beside 'Pound', but means a newly made-up word.
explanation.definitionFit: The New World is the Americas, the lands west of Europe.

clue.text: End in glut, unfortunately tending to spoil

indicators.note: something going unfortunately goes wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A feast closes in an unhappy surfeit, spoiling everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the letters of END IN GLUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgent parent or host is inclined to spoil others with treats.

clue.text: Guard wages

definitions.meaning: a prison guard, called a ... in British slang
pay, also called ... in old British slang

explanation.surface: A security officer's pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British slang both for a prison warder and for a person's wages or salary.

clue.text: Opera producer providing part for clever diva

indicators.note: only a part of these words is taken, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A composer writes a role for a talented soprano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' sounds like an operatic role, but it signals letters taken from CLEVER DIVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi composed operas such as Aida, so he is a producer of opera.

clue.text: Changed topic, as I'm easy to get on with

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone switches the subject, claiming to be agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' rearranges TOPIC AS IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico describes a likeable, congenial person who is pleasant company.

clue.text: Illness that doesn't make one feel great normally

definitions.text: Illness that doesn't make one feel great normally

parts.words: Illness that doesn't make one feel great normally
parts.note: a condition that makes a person feel great, but abnormally, in delusions of power

explanation.surface: A sickness that leaves one feeling below par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feel great' reads as 'feel well'; the illness makes one feel great, but abnormally, as grandiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Megalomania is a mental state marked by delusions of one's own greatness and power.

clue.text: Getting on train for Rugby, say

parts.note: boarding is getting on a vehicle such as a train
to train is to school or teach

explanation.surface: Catching a train to the town of Rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby looks like the town or sport; it is the famous English boarding school where the game began.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby School is an example of a residential private school in England.

clue.text: Is a Northern European allowed to love an old master?

parts.note: can means is allowed to
a Lett is a Latvian, from northern Europe
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Baltic citizen may adore a great painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Is a Lett allowed to love' inverts to 'Can a Lett love', so 'Is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter, one of the Old Masters.

clue.text: Regard boxer, perhaps, as protector

parts.note: to regard is to watch
a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Viewing a fighter as a defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter, but is the dog breed; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a guardian, whether a guard dog or an official body that protects standards.

clue.text: Its revelations are dated over four weeks before the present time

definitions.text: Its revelations are dated over four weeks before the present time

parts.words: Its revelations are dated over four weeks before the present time
parts.note: a card whose numbered doors are opened one per day through December before the Christmas presents

explanation.surface: Something whose disclosures are timed across a month leading up to now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present time' reads as now, but means the time of Christmas presents; the dated doors are opened through the four weeks of Advent.
explanation.definitionFit: Each little door of this seasonal calendar reveals a picture or chocolate on its date before Christmas.

clue.text: Criminal at home with revolutionary leader

parts.note: Pancho Villa led the Mexican Revolution
in means at home

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker indoors alongside a rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at home' looks like a villa, but gives IN; the villa is Pancho Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wrongdoer or criminal.

clue.text: State of unknown performing in operatic part

indicators.note: in means the unknown and performing go inside the operatic part

parts.note: an aria is a solo piece in an opera
z is an unknown quantity in algebra
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A condition of an unknown singer in an opera solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as a condition, but is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a state of the south-western United States.

clue.text: From within borders of Saxony, a German wine

indicators.note: within means the German sits inside those border letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr, so a German man

explanation.surface: A German man from Saxony with a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is a link word; the wine is fortified Spanish, not German.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from around Jerez in Spain.

clue.text: Place for spectacles of circular shape

definitions.text: Place for spectacles of circular shape

parts.words: Place for spectacles of circular shape
parts.note: not a case for round glasses but a round arena in Rome where spectacles, shows of gladiators, were staged

explanation.surface: A case for round glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' suggests eyeglasses; here it means public shows staged in a round Roman arena.
explanation.definitionFit: The great amphitheatre of ancient Rome, roughly round, hosted gladiatorial shows and other spectacles.

clue.text: Fish grouped in shallow water

definitions.meaning: a large group of fish swimming together
a stretch of sea made shallow by a sandbank

explanation.surface: Fish gathered in the shallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a large school of fish and also a sandbank making the water shallow.

clue.text: Port near northern Athens

parts.note: Edinburgh is nicknamed the Athens of the North, and its harbour district lies beside it

explanation.surface: A Greek harbour close to Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Athens suggests Piraeus, but 'northern Athens' is Edinburgh, the 'Athens of the North', whose port is on the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is the historic harbour area of Edinburgh, Scotland's capital, nicknamed the Athens of the North.

clue.text: Backed eccentric old proponent of zero tolerance

indicators.note: backed means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: a card is an eccentric, amusing person

explanation.surface: An odd former supporter of a strict crime policy is endorsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like 'supported', but reverses CARD + O, giving OCARD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco, the Athenian lawgiver, prescribed death for minor crimes, giving harshness without leniency.

clue.text: Type of red that makes good rouge, presumably

definitions.text: Type of red that makes good rouge, presumably

parts.words: Type of red that makes good rouge, presumably
parts.note: a red wine grape whose French name suggests black, which would presumably make good dark red make-up

explanation.surface: A shade of red ideal for make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rouge' looks like make-up, but is French for red wine; the grape's name means 'black pine', a playful reason it would make good dark rouge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir is a well-known red wine grape and the red wine made from it.

clue.text: Minimal amount a year as fee

parts.note: a p, a penny, is a minimal amount of money

explanation.surface: Paying a small annual charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is money given for work or services, akin to a charge or fee.

clue.text: An ugly novel about power and use of weapons

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram is placed around the next piece
novel means new, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An unattractive book on strength and armed conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but rearranges AN UGLY to GUNLAY, which goes 'about' P.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunplay is the firing of guns, especially in a shoot-out.

clue.text: Special case of a number reduced by 50 within month

parts.note: number in its shortened form is No

indicators.note: within means the fifty sits inside the month

parts.note: May is a month
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An exceptional instance of a figure cut by fifty during the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by 50' looks like subtraction, but 'reduced' abbreviates number to NO, and L goes 'within' MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something deviating from the norm, an exceptional or peculiar instance.
